Simmons was born in [Grapeland](/wiki/Grapeland,_Texas "Grapeland, Texas"), [Texas](/wiki/Texas "Texas"). She is the last of 12 children of Fanny (*née* Campbell) and Isaac Stubblefield.[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8) Her father was a [sharecropper](/wiki/Sharecropper "Sharecropper")[[9]](#cite_note-bloomberg_revives-a-black-college-9) up until the family moved to Houston during her school years. Her paternal grandfather descends partly from the Benza and [Kota people](/wiki/Kota_people_(Gabon) "Kota people (Gabon)"), enslaved people from [Gabon](/wiki/Gabon "Gabon"),[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11) while her maternal line is traced back to the [indigenous peoples of America](/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_America "Indigenous peoples of America").[[12]](#cite_note-12)

While in school, one of her teachers, Vernell Lillie, talked to her about attending college, something she had never considered before as a [first-generation college student](/wiki/First-generation_college_students_in_the_United_States "First-generation college students in the United States").[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14) She earned her [bachelor's degree](/wiki/Bachelor%27s_degree "Bachelor's degree"), on scholarship, from [Dillard University](/wiki/Dillard_University "Dillard University") in [New Orleans](/wiki/New_Orleans,_Louisiana "New Orleans, Louisiana"), [Louisiana](/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), in 1967. She earned her [master's](/wiki/Master%27s_degree "Master's degree") and a [doctorate](/wiki/Doctorate "Doctorate") in [Romance literature](/wiki/Romance_languages "Romance languages") from [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University") in 1970 and 1973, respectively.[[15]](#cite_note-thesis-simmons-1973-15)

The **economy of [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar")** is one of the highest in the world based on GDP per capita, ranking generally among the top ten richest countries on world rankings for 2015 and 2016 data compiled by the [World Bank](/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank"), the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), and the [International Monetary Fund](/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund") (IMF).[[13]](#cite_note-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14) [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") is sometimes considered as having a [mixed economy system](/wiki/Mixed_economy "Mixed economy").[[15]](#cite_note-15)

Qatar has the [world's third largest proven natural gas reserve](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_natural_gas_proven_reserves "List of countries by natural gas proven reserves") and is the [third-largest exporter of natural gas](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_natural_gas_exports "List of countries by natural gas exports").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Missouri_Bicentennial_13c_1976_issue.jpg/250px-Missouri_Bicentennial_13c_1976_issue.jpg)](/wiki/File:Missouri_Bicentennial_13c_1976_issue.jpg)

The Missouri state flag as depicted in the 1976 bicentennial postage stamp series.

The flag is a tricolor consisting of three horizontal stripes of red, white, and blue which resembles the flag of the [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). These represent valor, purity, vigilance, and justice. The colors also reflect the state's historic status as part of [French Louisiana](/wiki/Louisiana_(New_France) "Louisiana (New France)"). In the center white stripe is the [seal of Missouri](/wiki/Seal_of_Missouri "Seal of Missouri"), circled by a blue band containing 24 stars, symbolizing Missouri's admission as the 24th [U.S. state](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state").[[4]](#cite_note-mo.gov-5)

It is one of two U.S. state flags to feature a bear, the other being the flag of [California](/wiki/Flag_of_California "Flag of California"). It is also one of nine U.S. state flags to feature an eagle, alongside those of [Illinois](/wiki/Flag_of_Illinois "Flag of Illinois"), [Iowa](/wiki/Flag_of_Iowa "Flag of Iowa"), [Michigan](/wiki/Flag_of_Michigan "Flag of Michigan"), [New York](/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_New_York "Coat of arms of New York"), [North Dakota](/wiki/Flag_of_North_Dakota "Flag of North Dakota"), [Oregon](/wiki/Flag_of_Oregon "Flag of Oregon"), [Pennsylvania](/wiki/Flag_of_Pennsylvania "Flag of Pennsylvania"), and [Wyoming](/wiki/Flag_of_Wyoming "Flag of Wyoming").

In 2001, the [North American Vexillological Association](/wiki/North_American_Vexillological_Association "North American Vexillological Association") surveyed its members on the designs of the 72 [U.S. state](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), [U.S. territorial](/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States") and [Canadian provincial](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") flags. The Missouri flag ranked in the bottom 25, 48th out of the 72.[[5]](#cite_note-6)

The planet's rotation makes it an oblate [spheroid](/wiki/Spheroid "Spheroid"), which is [flattened](/wiki/Flattening "Flattening") at the [poles](/wiki/Geographical_pole "Geographical pole") and [bulging](/wiki/Equatorial_bulge "Equatorial bulge") at the [equator](/wiki/Equator "Equator"). Its equatorial radius is more than 10% longer than the polar radius: 60,268 km (37,449 mi) versus 54,364 km (33,780 mi).[[6]](#cite_note-fact-7) [Jupiter](/wiki/Jupiter "Jupiter"), [Uranus](/wiki/Uranus "Uranus"), and [Neptune](/wiki/Neptune "Neptune"), the other giant planets in the Solar System, are less oblate. The combination of the bulge and the rotation rate means that the effective surface gravity along the equator, 8.96 m/s2 (29.4 ft/s2), is 74% of what it is at the poles and is lower than the surface gravity of Earth. However, the equatorial [escape velocity](/wiki/Escape_velocity "Escape velocity"), nearly 36 km/s (22 mi/s; 130,000 km/h; 81,000 mph), is much higher than that of Earth.[[62]](#cite_note-Gregersen2010-64)

The lower region of the valley receives less rainfall than the upper regions of the south; the lower boroughs of [Iztapalapa](/wiki/Iztapalapa "Iztapalapa"), [Iztacalco](/wiki/Iztacalco "Iztacalco"), [Venustiano Carranza](/wiki/Venustiano_Carranza,_D.F. "Venustiano Carranza, D.F.") and the east portion of [Gustavo A. Madero](/wiki/Gustavo_A._Madero,_D.F. "Gustavo A. Madero, D.F.") are usually drier and warmer than the upper southern boroughs of [Tlalpan](/wiki/Tlalpan "Tlalpan") and [Milpa Alta](/wiki/Milpa_Alta "Milpa Alta"), a mountainous region of [pine](/wiki/Pine "Pine") and [oak](/wiki/Oak "Oak") trees known as the range of [Ajusco](/wiki/Ajusco "Ajusco"). The average annual temperature varies from 12 to 16 °C (54 to 61 °F), depending on the altitude of the borough. The temperature is rarely below 3 °C (37 °F) or above 30 °C (86 °F).[[100]](#cite_note-weatherspark-104) At the Tacubaya observatory, the lowest temperature ever registered was −4.4 °C (24 °F) on 13 February 1960, and the highest temperature on record was 34.7 °C (94.5 °F) on 25 May 2024.[[101]](#cite_note-105) Overall precipitation is heavily concentrated in the summer months, and includes dense [hail](/wiki/Hail "Hail").

Snow falls in the city scarcely, although somewhat more often on nearby mountaintops. Throughout its history, the Central Valley of Mexico was accustomed to having several snowfalls per decade (including a period between 1878 and 1895 in which every single year—except 1880—recorded snowfalls[[102]](#cite_note-Clima-CDMX-106)), mostly [lake-effect snow](/wiki/Lake-effect_snow "Lake-effect snow"). The Cardinals' drafting of [Tim Hightower](/wiki/Tim_Hightower "Tim Hightower") in 2008 resulted in Arrington being shifted to third place on the depth chart at running back. He became the team's principal kick returner and in [Super Bowl XLIII](/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIII "Super Bowl XLIII") caught 2 passes for 35 yards.

The battle began around 8 a.m. with the first allied column attacking the village of Telnitz, which was defended by the 3rd Line Regiment. This sector of the battlefield witnessed heavy action in the following moments as several ferocious Allied charges evicted the French from the town and forced them on the other side of the Goldbach. The first men of Davout's corps arrived at this time and threw the Allies out of Telnitz before they too were attacked by [hussars](/wiki/Hussar "Hussar") and re-abandoned the town. Additional Allied attacks out of Telnitz were checked by French artillery.
Allied columns started pouring against the French right, but not at the desired speed, so the French were mostly successful in curbing the attacks. In reality, the Allied deployments were mistaken and poorly timed: cavalry detachments under [Liechtenstein](/wiki/Johann_I_Josef,_Prince_of_Liechtenstein "Johann I Josef, Prince of Liechtenstein") on the Allied left flank had to be placed in the right flank and in the process they ran into and slowed down part of the second column of infantry that was advancing towards the French right. At the time, the planners thought this was a disaster, but later on it helped the Allies. Meanwhile, the lead elements of the second column were attacking the village of Sokolnitz, which was defended by the 26th Light Regiment and the *Tirailleurs*, French skirmishers. Initial Allied assaults proved unsuccessful and General [Langeron](/wiki/Louis_Alexandre_Andrault_de_Langeron "Louis Alexandre Andrault de Langeron") ordered the bombardment of the village. This deadly barrage forced the French out, and around the same time, the third column attacked the castle of Sokolnitz. The French, however, counterattacked and regained the village, only to be thrown out again. Conflict in this area ended momentarily when [Friant](/wiki/Louis_Friant "Louis Friant")'s division (part of III Corps) retook the village. Posing as an emissary of the college, Bond meets Blofeld, who has established a clinical allergy-research institute atop [Piz Gloria](/wiki/Piz_Gloria "Piz Gloria") in the [Swiss Alps](/wiki/Swiss_Alps "Swiss Alps"). Bond soon establishes that Blofeld is [brainwashing](/wiki/Brainwashing "Brainwashing") his patients to distribute bacteriological warfare agents throughout various parts of the world.

Bond escapes from the clinic after Blofeld identifies him as a British agent. Bond arranges a raid on the clinic using men from Draco's organisation. The raid is a success, although Blofeld escapes. Bond marries Tracy, but she is murdered shortly afterwards by Irma Bunt, Blofeld's partner.

It was discovered by [Friedrich Oskar Giesel](/wiki/Friedrich_Oskar_Giesel "Friedrich Oskar Giesel") in 1902, who gave it the name *emanium*; the element got its name by being wrongly identified with a substance [André-Louis Debierne](/wiki/Andr%C3%A9-Louis_Debierne "André-Louis Debierne") found in 1899 and called actinium. The [actinide](/wiki/Actinide "Actinide") series, a set of 15 elements between actinium and [lawrencium](/wiki/Lawrencium "Lawrencium") in the [periodic table](/wiki/Periodic_table "Periodic table"), is named after actinium. Together with [polonium](/wiki/Polonium "Polonium"), [radium](/wiki/Radium "Radium"), and [radon](/wiki/Radon "Radon"), actinium was one of the first [non-primordial radioactive elements](/wiki/Primordial_element "Primordial element") to be discovered.

A soft, silvery-white [radioactive](/wiki/Radioactive "Radioactive") metal, actinium reacts rapidly with [oxygen](/wiki/Oxygen "Oxygen") and moisture in air, forming a white coating of actinium oxide that prevents further oxidation. As with most [lanthanides](/wiki/Lanthanide "Lanthanide") and many [actinides](/wiki/Actinide "Actinide"), actinium assumes [oxidation state](/wiki/Oxidation_state "Oxidation state") +3 in nearly all its chemical compounds. Actinium is found only in traces in [uranium](/wiki/Uranium "Uranium") and [thorium](/wiki/Thorium "Thorium") ores as the [isotope](/wiki/Isotope "Isotope") 227Ac, which decays with a [half-life](/wiki/Half-life "Half-life") of 21.772 years, predominantly emitting [beta](/wiki/Beta_particle "Beta particle") and sometimes [alpha particles](/wiki/Alpha_particle "Alpha particle"), and 228Ac, which is beta active with a half-life of 6.15 hours. Lewandowski began his international career with Poland [under-19](/wiki/Poland_national_under-19_football_team "Poland national under-19 football team") in 2007.[[263]](#cite_note-264) He would also make three appearances for [Poland's U21 team](/wiki/Poland_national_under-21_football_team "Poland national under-21 football team"), in friendly matches against [England](/wiki/England_national_under-21_football_team "England national under-21 football team"), [Belarus](/wiki/Belarus_national_under-21_football_team "Belarus national under-21 football team") and [Finland](/wiki/Finland_national_under-21_football_team "Finland national under-21 football team").

His debut for the senior national team came on 10 September 2008, three weeks after his 20th birthday, against [San Marino](/wiki/San_Marino_national_football_team "San Marino national football team") where he came on as a substitute and scored a goal in a 2–0 away win in [2010 FIFA World Cup qualification](/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2010 FIFA World Cup qualification").[[264]](#cite_note-265) Only [Włodzimierz Lubański](/wiki/W%C5%82odzimierz_Luba%C5%84ski "Włodzimierz Lubański") scored a goal on his debut for the national team at a younger age than Lewandowski, having been 16 at the time. Lewandowski scored another qualifying goal against the same team on 1 April 2009, in a 10–0 victory.[[265]](#cite_note-266)
